stem: What is the purpose of the process of controlling a stage?
answer: To assign work, monitor it and take corrective action so that the stage stays within its tolerances
distractors: To assign work packages, monitor the team's output and report the completion of each product to the users
To monitor the stage against its plan, escalate every deviation to the project board and revise the tolerances
To handle issues and risks, keep the business case current and confirm that the expected benefits have been realized
To assign work, monitor progress and take corrective action so that the project stays within the business layer's tolerances
To report progress to the project board, take corrective action and prepare the plan for the next stage
To monitor the work of team managers, accept their products and authorize the closure of the project
explanation: The purpose covers assigning work, monitoring it, handling issues, reporting progress to the board and correcting the course of the stage within the tolerances the board set. Escalating every deviation, revising the tolerances and confirming benefits all belong elsewhere; the project manager works within tolerances rather than changing them.

stem: How does the purpose of controlling a stage differ from that of managing product delivery?
answer: Controlling a stage keeps the stage within tolerances, while managing product delivery accepts, executes and delivers work
distractors: Controlling a stage produces, reviews and accepts the specialist products, while managing product delivery only reports progress
Controlling a stage prepares the next stage plan, while managing product delivery approves, funds and monitors the current plan
Controlling a stage owns the business case, while managing product delivery owns the benefits management approach and the plans
Controlling a stage is used only on linear projects, while managing product delivery is used only on agile and hybrid projects
Controlling a stage sets project tolerances, while managing product delivery sets stage tolerances for the board and the manager
Controlling a stage reports to the business layer, while managing product delivery reports to the project board and assurance
explanation: Controlling a stage is the project manager's day-to-day management of the stage, keeping it within the board's tolerances, while the team-side process is where work packages are accepted, the work is done and the products are delivered. The two processes meet at the work package, not at the stage plan.

stem: Which of these is an objective of the process of controlling a stage?
answer: That the business case is kept under review throughout the stage
distractors: That the project plan is kept under review and re-baselined at each stage boundary
That the stage's products are handed over to the users and their benefits confirmed
That the project board authorizes each stage before any work begins
That the tolerances for team managers are agreed with the business layer
That the project's approach to quality is defined and baselined
That the project mandate is reviewed before the stage plan is produced
explanation: The objectives include keeping the business case under review, alongside focusing attention on the stage's products, controlling risks and issues, meeting quality expectations and working within tolerances. Re-baselining the project plan and confirming benefits belong to later processes, and defining the quality approach happens during initiation.

stem: Which of these is NOT an objective of the process of controlling a stage?
answer: To confirm that the board has authorized the next stage
distractors: To ensure that risks and issues are controlled
To ensure that the business case is kept under review
To ensure that the agreed products for the stage meet the agreed quality expectations and are accepted
explanation: The objectives are about controlling risks and issues, reviewing the business case, meeting the stage's quality expectations, keeping attention on the agreed products and working within tolerances. Obtaining authority for the next stage, and the resources for it, is the purpose of managing a stage boundary.

stem: PRINCE2 says the project manager acts as a facilitator rather than a controller in this process. What does that mean in practice?
answer: Giving team managers freedom within their tolerances, so that escalations are kept to a minimum
distractors: Approving every task a team member performs, so that no unauthorized work takes place at all
Escalating all issues and risks to the project board as soon as they are identified
Delegating the stage plan and the highlight reports to the team managers
Keeping the stage plan away from the team so that they concentrate on their own work packages
Declining to set tolerances, because tolerances prevent the team from learning
Chairing the project board so that decisions can be taken more quickly
explanation: The point of tolerances is to give people room to act: team managers should have freedom where possible, and the project manager should discuss their own tolerances with the board to gain freedom to act and learn. Approving every task, or escalating everything, removes that freedom and defeats the purpose.

stem: When is the process of controlling a stage used?
answer: In every stage, normally for the first time after the project board has authorized the project
distractors: Only in the final stage, because earlier stages are covered by the initiation stage
Once per project, immediately after the project mandate has been received
Only between stage boundaries, and never during the initiation stage
Only once the project board has approved an exception plan for the stage
Only on projects that use a linear rather than an iterative delivery method
At each stage boundary, in place of the process of managing a stage boundary
explanation: Controlling a stage describes the project manager's day-to-day management of a stage and is used for each stage of the project. It is normally used first once the board has authorized the project, though it can also be used during initiation on large or complex projects.

stem: A large, complex project has a long and demanding initiation stage. What does PRINCE2 allow here?
answer: Controlling a stage can be used during the initiation stage, especially for large projects
distractors: Controlling a stage cannot begin until the board has authorized the first delivery stage
Controlling a stage is used, but only to escalate issues, because no work packages exist yet
Controlling a stage replaces initiating a project above a defined size threshold
Controlling a stage may be used only if the board delegates its authority to the project manager
Controlling a stage may be used only after all initiation documentation has been baselined
Controlling a stage is used, but the initiation stage is then reported as a delivery stage
explanation: Although the process normally starts after project authorization, the manual notes it can be used during the initiation stage, particularly where the project is large or complex. That is a matter of scale and complexity, not of the board delegating its authority.

topic: Work packages when the project manager is team manager
stem: On a small project the project manager also takes the team manager role. What does PRINCE2 say about work package descriptions?
answer: They are still used to define and control the work, with team manager read as the individual
distractors: They are no longer needed, because the project manager already knows what the work involves
A separate team manager must be appointed before any work can be authorized
The stage plan replaces the work package descriptions for the whole stage
Checkpoint reports are replaced by the highlight report sent to the project board
The project board must approve each individual task before it can start
Team plans remain mandatory, but work package descriptions become optional
explanation: Work package descriptions are the vehicle for defining, assigning and controlling work and for setting tolerances, so they are still used when the project manager does both roles. In that case the references to the team manager apply to the individual team member given the work.

stem: At the end of the last stage of a project, what does controlling a stage trigger?
answer: Closing a project, whereas other stage ends trigger managing a stage boundary
distractors: Managing a stage boundary, exactly as it does at the end of every other stage
Directing a project, which then triggers managing a stage boundary
Managing product delivery, so that the last work package can be closed down
Starting up a project, so that lessons can be captured for the next project
Initiating a project, so that the next stage can be authorized by the board
explanation: The activities of managing a stage boundary happen towards the end of each stage with the exception of the final stage. There, controlling a stage hands over to closing a project instead, so that the project can be brought to a controlled close.

topic: Triggers to authorize a work package
stem: Which of these is a trigger for the project manager to authorize a work package?
answer: The project board approving an exception plan for the stage
distractors: A team manager submitting a checkpoint report for the period
A stakeholder requesting a copy of the latest highlight report
The completion of a quality review for one of the stage's products
The project manager adding a new entry to the lessons log
Project support circulating the minutes of a progress meeting
The quality register being updated with a planned review
explanation: The triggers are stage authorization, an approved exception plan, a new work package arising from evaluating stage status, and corrective action taken in response to an issue or risk. A checkpoint report feeds the evaluation of work package status, and a completed quality review belongs to receiving a finished work package.

stem: Which set of actions belongs to authorizing a work package?
answer: Co-creating and reviewing the work package description with the team manager, and consulting project assurance on the reviewers
distractors: Checking the quality register for completed reviews, then marking the work package complete in the stage plan
Comparing actual progress with the stage plan, deciding whether corrective action is needed, and recording the decision in the log
Preparing an exception report, putting recovery options to the project board, and recording its decision in the project log
Compiling the highlight report from checkpoint reports, the project log, and the stage plan, and issuing it to the board
Assessing each recovery option against the business case, selecting one, and escalating it to the board
Updating the risk register, escalating any risk that exceeds the stage tolerance, and informing the board of the action
explanation: Authorization is a joint exercise with the team manager: the description is defined and reviewed together, the team manager's acceptance confirmed, and the quality reviewers checked with assurance before work starts. Checking completed reviews and marking work complete belong to receiving a completed work package.

stem: A work package should cover the creation of one or more products. What does PRINCE2 recommend when a single product needs more work than one work package can hold?
answer: Break the product down into sub-products, each with its own product description
distractors: Authorize one work package and record the outstanding work as an issue in the project log
Split the product between teams without product descriptions, to keep the package simple
Ask the project board to widen the stage tolerance so that the work fits a single package
Treat the extra work as a change and let the team manager approve it
Issue a new project mandate covering the additional work before authorization
Move the whole product into the next stage and report it as unfinished
explanation: If a product requires more than one work package, it is broken down into sub-products with their own product descriptions, so each work package still covers coherent, defined products. Widening tolerances or leaving the work undefined simply hides the problem.

topic: Progress information for a work package
stem: Which management product provides the progress information reviewed when evaluating work package status?
answer: The checkpoint report for the work package
distractors: The highlight report for the previous reporting period
The end stage report from the previous stage
The exception report raised for the current stage
The business case for the project
The communication management approach
The product description for the end product
explanation: Evaluating work package status draws on the checkpoint report for the work package in progress, together with informal conversations with the team manager. The highlight report is the project manager's output to the board, not an input to this activity.

stem: After evaluating work package status, which plan does the project manager update with actuals to date, forecasts and adjustments?
answer: The stage plan for the current stage
distractors: The project plan for the whole project
The team plan maintained by the team manager
The product description for each product in the work package
The communication management approach
The benefits management approach
The business case
explanation: The activity keeps the stage plan current by recording actuals to date, forecasts and any adjustments. The team plan belongs to the team manager, and the project plan is updated at the stage boundary rather than in this day-to-day activity.

stem: Before accepting a completed work package, which check does PRINCE2 require the project manager to make?
answer: Check the quality register to confirm the necessary quality reviews have been completed
distractors: Check that the team manager has entered the actual cost in the project plan
Check that the project board has approved the work package description
Check that the highlight report for the period has been distributed
Check that the risk register holds no open risks against the products
Check that the stage tolerance has been re-baselined by the project board
Check that the checkpoint reports have been filed in the project log
explanation: Receiving a completed work package is a confirmation step: the work must match the description and the quality register must show the required reviews were completed. Approval of the description happens at authorization, not at completion.

stem: The project manager has confirmed that each product in the work package has gained its requisite approval. What must happen next?
answer: Confirm the product register record for each approved product is updated, then update the stage plan
distractors: Ask the project board to authorize the next work package before any records are changed
Close the project log entry and archive the product descriptions, then report to the board
Raise an exception report explaining the completion to the project board
Record the completion in the lessons log and remove the products from the product register, then update the plan
Re-baseline the stage plan, because completion changes the plan's baseline
Ask project assurance to re-run the quality reviews before the work is accepted
explanation: The remaining steps are to confirm the product register reflects each approved product and to show the work package as complete in the stage plan. Re-baselining is not warranted by planned completion, and approval has already been checked.

stem: A team is delivering a work package using an agile approach. What does PRINCE2 say must have happened for the project manager to accept it as complete?
answer: The team manager has delivered the features agreed for the timebox in full
distractors: A product description has been written for every item in the product backlog
Every quality review listed in the project plan for the stage has been held
The product owner has approved the stage plan for the current stage
The work package has been closed in the product register before the end of the sprint
The full scope of the product has been delivered, regardless of the timebox
The team manager has re-estimated the remaining work for the next timebox
explanation: The confirmation required is that the work defined in the description has been done or, where an agile approach is used, that the features agreed for the timebox have been delivered. Completion is measured against what was agreed, not against the whole backlog or a future timebox.

stem: What is the objective of the activity evaluate stage status?
answer: To maintain an accurate and current picture of progress on the work performed and the status of resources
distractors: To record every issue and risk raised during the stage in the project log, and review them weekly
To produce the highlight report for the current reporting period, and send it to the project board
To decide whether an exception report should be raised to the board, and what it should contain
To confirm that each completed work package meets its quality criteria, and is ready for handover
To authorize the next work package required by the stage plan, and agree its tolerances with the team
To collect the checkpoint reports issued by the team managers, and file them in the project log
explanation: The activity exists to keep an accurate, current view of progress and of resource status, so that decisions are based on comparing what happened with what was expected. Producing the highlight report is a separate activity that draws on this one.

stem: How often does the project manager evaluate stage status?
answer: At a frequency defined in the stage plan, and also when triggered by board advice or a new issue
distractors: Only at each stage boundary, as part of preparing the next stage plan, and the end stage report for the board
At the frequency set out in the project's communication management approach
Whenever a checkpoint report arrives from a team manager, and on the dates in the project plan
Only when the project manager suspects that a tolerance may be breached
Continuously, because a formal review would slow the team down, and delay the work
Once, when the stage plan is authorized, with no further reviews
explanation: The stage plan sets the rhythm, but the activity can also be prompted by the board's advice or by analyzing a new issue or risk. Reacting only to checkpoint reports would leave the aggregated view of the stage unchecked.

stem: While evaluating stage status, the project manager confirms that ownership of two products has passed to the users. How does PRINCE2 treat this?
answer: As a phased handover, which may happen more than once during the lifecycle
distractors: As a stage boundary, which must be reported in the end stage report before it occurs
As project closure, which ends the project as soon as the first product is transferred
As a change of scope, which needs the change authority's approval
As benefit realization, which is recorded in the benefits management approach
As a quality failure, because products left the project's control before acceptance
As an exception, because ownership cannot transfer before the final stage
explanation: The activity includes confirming whether ownership of any products has been transferred to users as part of a phased handover, and the manual notes that there may be several handovers during the lifecycle. That is different from closing the project, which happens once.

stem: An issue is raised in the middle of a stage. According to PRINCE2, what must happen before a course of action is decided?
answer: The issue is registered in the project log and then assessed for its impact
distractors: The issue is escalated to the project board so that it can decide the response
An exception report is raised so that a replacement stage plan can be produced
The team manager is told to stop work until the issue has been resolved
The issue is entered in the lessons log and work continues on the current package
The issue is added to the next highlight report for the board's information
The issue is passed to project assurance to confirm whether it is genuine
explanation: Each issue or risk is registered in the project log and then assessed for its impact before any decision on a course of action. Escalation, exception reporting and stopping work are all responses that may follow the assessment, not steps that replace it.

topic: Who may raise issues and risks
stem: Which statement about raising issues and risks during a stage is correct?
answer: Any business member, project member or other stakeholder may raise one, captured consistently
distractors: Only the project manager and team managers may raise one, and only through checkpoint reports
Only project board members may raise one, and only at the frequency set in the stage plan
Anyone may raise one, but only those affecting cost are entered in the project log
Anyone may raise one, but capture is deferred to the next stage boundary review
Only the roles named in the communication management approach, using its format
Only the project manager may raise one, because they own the project log
explanation: Issues and risks arrive in an unstructured way from anyone in the business, the project or the wider stakeholder group, so capture has to be consistent and reliable. The manual also stresses psychological safety, so that people feel able to raise concerns without fear.

stem: What is the objective when the project manager takes corrective action?
answer: To select and implement actions that resolve deviations within the stage and project tolerances
distractors: To record every deviation in the project log for the project board's information
To change the stage plan baseline so that the deviation no longer appears
To escalate the deviation to the project board as soon as it is forecast
To prevent any change to the plan, so that the original baseline is preserved
To move work between team managers until the tolerances are met, and the plan is updated each week
To reduce the scope of the stage so that the forecast returns within tolerance
explanation: Corrective action resolves deviations within the tolerances already agreed for the stage and project. Re-baselining, cutting scope or escalating are different responses, and escalation is reserved for deviations that cannot be resolved inside those tolerances.

stem: How is the selected corrective action actually triggered in this process?
answer: By authorizing a work package that carries out the corrective action
distractors: By raising an exception report for the project board's approval
By updating the business case and issuing a revised highlight report
By asking the team manager to amend the team plan
By closing the current stage and starting a new one
By escalating the issue or risk to the business layer
By recording the deviation in the lessons log
explanation: The manual links the two activities directly: corrective action is triggered by authorizing a work package. That keeps the response inside the same controlled mechanism used for any other work.

stem: Corrective action will require one of the stage's products to change. Which records does PRINCE2 say the project manager updates?
answer: The product register records of the affected products, showing required changes, and the issue report
distractors: The project mandate and the outline business case, because the scope has altered
The communication management approach and the benefits management approach, because the change affects them
The team plan only, because the stage plan is unaffected by corrective action, and the board's records
The quality register only, because a product change creates a quality activity
The project log only, because the product register is updated at the stage boundary
The product descriptions only, because the register records delivery not change
explanation: Corrective action updates the product register records of the affected products, including whether changes or new products are needed, and the issue report where one exists so that its status reflects the action. The stage plan and project log are also updated, but neither replaces the product register.

stem: When does the activity escalate issues and risks apply?
answer: When no corrective action within the manager's control would keep the stage within tolerances
distractors: When an issue or risk is raised by someone outside the project management team
When the project board has asked the project manager for advice on an issue
When a checkpoint report shows that a task is running behind schedule
When the project manager has delegated part of their tolerance to a team manager
When a single issue or risk affects more than one work package
When the stage plan has been updated with actuals more than once in a period
explanation: Escalation applies where corrective action inside the project manager's control cannot prevent the stage, or the project, from breaching the board's tolerances. It covers all types of issue and risk, including aggregations of them, and is not triggered merely by a late task.

stem: Why does PRINCE2 suggest that escalation may be carried out in two steps?
answer: Because an exception report takes time to assemble, so the board is warned early and then receives it
distractors: Because the board must approve the exception report before the project manager writes it
Because an exception report may only be raised once the tolerance has actually been breached
Because the business layer must be told before the project board is informed
Because the team manager must replan the affected work package first, and the project manager approve it
Because the two steps mirror the actuals and forecasts in the stage plan
Because the project manager must seek the board's advice before analyzing the deviation
explanation: Gathering the evidence for an exception report takes time, so the manual recommends alerting the board to the forecast exception situation as early as possible and following it with the report. Early warning gives more time to implement corrective action.

stem: What does the project manager put to the project board when escalating, and what happens next?
answer: An exception report giving the situation, the options and a recommendation, on which the board decides
distractors: A highlight report describing the deviation, which the board notes for information only
An end stage report, which the board approves before the next stage is planned
An issue report, which the board forwards to the business layer for a decision
A checkpoint report, which the board uses to reset the stage tolerances, and the work packages
A revised business case, which the board approves before any recovery work starts, and funds
A work package description, which the board authorizes in place of the project manager
explanation: The exception report sets out the situation, the recovery options and the project manager's recommendation, and the board then decides what to do. The board is free to support or reject the recommendation, and the project manager executes the decision.

topic: Corrective actions in the highlight report
stem: Why does the highlight report include a list of the corrective actions taken during the reporting period?
answer: To assure the board that the manager is acting within tolerances
distractors: To allow the board to approve each corrective action retrospectively
To record the lessons that will be reviewed at the end of the stage
To bring the product register up to date with the status of each product
To show that the stage plan has been re-baselined during the period
To meet the business layer's requirement for a benefits update
To justify any change to the tolerances that the board has agreed
explanation: Listing the corrective actions gives the board visible evidence that the stage is being managed within tolerance between formal reviews. Approval of individual actions is not the purpose; that would remove the delegated freedom the tolerances exist to provide.

stem: Where is the frequency of highlight reporting defined, and how may reporting work on an agile project?
answer: In the communication management approach, and on an agile project it may work as a pull system where the board views progress charts
distractors: In the stage plan, and on an agile project it is replaced by the sprint review, held by the delivery team each fortnight
In the business case, and on an agile project it is issued at timebox boundaries only
In the project initiation documentation, and on an agile project it becomes optional, if the board agrees
In the risk management approach, and on an agile project it is replaced by the risk register, kept by the team
In the highlight report itself, and on an agile project it follows the delivery team's calendar, as agreed with the board
In the project board's terms of reference, and on an agile project it is issued on request, by the manager
explanation: The board defines the reporting frequency in the communication management approach, and other information goes to stakeholders at that cadence. With an iterative-incremental delivery method the highlight report may rely on a pull system, with the board reading progress charts rather than waiting for a pushed report.

stem: How does PRINCE2 describe the relationship between the project manager, project support and team managers during this process?
answer: Collaborative, with the project manager facilitating rather than assigning, so ownership improves
distractors: Directive, with the project manager instructing team managers on how each task should be performed
Independent, with each role reporting its own progress directly to the project board
Contractual, with the relationship governed only by the work package description
Hierarchical, with project support directing team managers on the project manager's behalf
Optional, with collaboration needed only where the supplier is externally contracted
Competitive, with team managers bidding for the next work package, and the project manager choosing
explanation: The manual is explicit that the relationship should be collaborative: the project manager facilitates rather than delegates or assigns, so that team managers and project support take ownership of their contribution. A purely directive or contractual reading misses the point of the work package relationship.

stem: The project manager lacks the specialist knowledge to define the products and method statements in a work package description. What does PRINCE2 allow?
answer: The work may be delegated, for example to the team manager or specialists, but the manager retains responsibility
distractors: Responsibility passes to the team manager, who becomes accountable for the description
The work package description must be written by project assurance to keep it independent
The specialist content may be left out until the team manager starts the work, and added later
The project board must approve the description before any delegation happens, and then sign it
The work package is not needed where the project manager lacks the expertise, and the team manager decides
The description is replaced by the relevant section of the project plan, and the stage plan
explanation: PRINCE2 shows the project manager as responsible for creating the new management products but allows the tasks to be delegated while responsibility is retained. The project manager's role becomes making sure the content is properly defined, reviewed and assured for the stage plan's needs.

stem: In the RACI chart for controlling a stage, what does the note A1 record?
answer: That the project manager is accountable for the team's corrective actions
distractors: That the project manager is accountable for all corrective action in the project
That the team manager is accountable for corrective actions at team level
That project assurance is accountable for reviewing every corrective action
That the project board is accountable for corrective action that breaches a tolerance
That the project manager is responsible for their own corrective actions only
explanation: A1 sits against the project manager and records accountability for the corrective actions the team manager takes, while R3 records responsibility for the project manager's own corrective actions. Accountability for actions at team level stays with the project manager, not with the team manager.

topic: RACI for capturing issues and risks
stem: In the RACI chart, the notes R1 and R2 both relate to capturing issues and risks. What do they distinguish?
answer: R1 is capturing issues and risks at stage level and R2 the same responsibility at team level
distractors: R1 is responsibility for assessing issues and R2 responsibility for assessing risks
R1 is responsibility for risks that are threats and R2 responsibility for opportunities
R1 is responsibility for issues raised inside the project and R2 for those raised outside
R1 is responsibility for capturing in the project log and R2 for capturing in the risk register
R1 is accountability for the project log and R2 responsibility for the lessons log
explanation: The chart splits the responsibility by level: the stage-level capture of issues and risks is distinguished from capture at team level, reflecting that both the project manager and the team manager contribute. The split is about where the capture happens, not about the type of issue or risk.

stem: What is true of the business case while a stage is being controlled?
answer: It is checked regularly to confirm that it remains viable, and the board must be told if not
distractors: It is re-baselined at each stage boundary by the project manager, and approved by the project board
It is reviewed only when the project board asks for an exception plan
It is delegated to the team managers, who confirm the benefits after handover
It is updated whenever a work package is authorized, to show the spend to date
It is checked once, when the stage plan is approved by the board, and then filed with the plan
It is replaced by the benefits management approach once delivery starts
explanation: The business case practice is applied by checking viability regularly during the stage, with the board informed if the justification no longer holds. The benefits and sustainability management approaches are also applied, and their requirements are built into the stage's work package descriptions.
